methodological_rigor.justification: NEOTERIC is a randomized phase II trial with an appropriate 1:1 randomization and a safety run-in phase, but comparison of efficacy is against historical controls (15% pCR) rather than between the two arms. The sample size calculation is based on the Atezo+Tira arm only. No formal comparison between the two treatment arms is performed, and the study was not powered for arm-to-arm comparison. The ITT analysis is correctly defined. There is one protocol deviation (a patient in the Atezo arm received Atezo+Tira) and one patient who declined surgery, handled appropriately with ITT and mITT analyses. The follow-up period (median 21.5 months) is short for survival outcomes in LARC.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: NEOTERIC addresses the important question of whether TIGIT/PD-L1 dual blockade after nCRT can improve pCR rates in pMMR/MSS LARC, which typically responds poorly to immunotherapy alone. The 35.7% pCR rate in the Atezo+Tira arm is clinically meaningful against a historical 15% benchmark. However, the comparison to historical controls rather than a concurrent control group, the single-country design (China), and the short follow-up limit clinical translation. The evolving total neoadjuvant therapy landscape provides context but also competing alternatives. The biomarker data (PD-L1, TIGIT, PVR) are exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript provides a CONSORT flow diagram with transparent disclosure of the protocol deviation and surgery declination. Endpoints are clearly defined. Safety data are comprehensively reported by treatment component (RT/CT, immunotherapy, surgery). The historical control comparison methodology is clearly stated (15% from prior literature). Biomarker analyses are described with appropriate antibodies and platforms. No data are publicly shared. The statistical approach of comparing to historical controls using normal approximation to binomial test is standard for single-arm designs but applying it to only one arm of a randomized trial is an unconventional hybrid approach.

novelty_literature.justification: This is the first globally reported randomized phase II trial of anti-TIGIT (tiragolumab) in combination with PD-L1 blockade (atezolizumab) after nCRT in LARC, specifically in pMMR/MSS tumors. The finding of 35.7% pCR in a population where ICI monotherapy typically shows limited activity is novel and mechanistically interesting. The first-in-class application of TIGIT+PD-L1 dual blockade in the neoadjuvant rectal cancer setting, with associated biomarker data (TIGIT, PVR, PD-L1), represents a genuine advance in an area of active investigation.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with clear presentation of the study design, safety run-in rationale, and efficacy results. The limitations section appropriately acknowledges short follow-up, small sample size for biomarker analyses, and the historical control comparison. The discussion contextualizes findings within the broader LARC treatment landscape (TNT, RAPIDO, PRODIGE 23) with appropriate cross-trial caution. The mechanistic rationale for radiotherapy-ICI synergy and TIGIT-PD-L1 combination is well-explained. Minor weakness: the discussion of pCR as a surrogate for survival is appropriately nuanced.

key_strengths: First globally reported randomized trial of TIGIT+PD-L1 dual blockade after nCRT in pMMR/MSS LARC, achieving 35.7% pCR versus 15% historical control (P=0.002)
Well-designed with safety run-in phase, transparent protocol deviation reporting, and comprehensive safety reporting by treatment component
Exploratory biomarker analyses of PD-L1, TIGIT, and PVR provide mechanistic context and hypothesis-generating data for future patient selection
Acceptable safety profile with grade ≥3 Atezo/Tira-related AEs in only 10-11% despite all-pMMR/MSS patient population
key_concerns: Efficacy is compared against historical controls (15%) rather than between the two randomized arms, making the study's primary design rationale—the comparison between Atezo+Tira vs Atezo—statistically underpowered
Short median follow-up (21.5 months) is insufficient to assess survival outcomes in LARC; pCR's value as a surrogate endpoint remains debated
Single-country (China) design with five centers limits generalizability to Western populations with different baseline characteristics and treatment practices
No formal comparison between arms; the higher pCR with combination (35.7%) vs monotherapy (22.2%) is not statistically tested and could be due to chance with n=55
chief_reviewer.rationale: NEOTERIC is an important proof-of-concept study demonstrating feasibility and preliminary efficacy of dual TIGIT+PD-L1 blockade after nCRT in pMMR/MSS LARC. The 35.7% pCR rate exceeds historical benchmarks, but the historical control design, single-country setting, small sample size, and short follow-up limit conclusions. Tier 3 is appropriate for this well-executed but exploratory randomized phase II study, with minor revisions needed to clarify the hybrid randomized/historical control design rationale.
